model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.note: Model identity is the actual runtime model of the evaluating session, taken from the session environment (claude-opus-5[1m], Opus 5 with 1M context), not the claude-fable-5 template text in the agent definition.

issues_detected.description: The record documents extensive format conversion (Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt to DICOM, Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, ECG .xml to WFDB, OMOP CDM mapping) but the software_and_tools slot is absent and no conversion tool, pipeline or version is named anywhere. Tools appear only incidentally in other slots: REDCap for capture and e-consent, the MoCA Duo application, the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard via dqd_omop.json, github.com/AI-READI, and FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure. Not one software version number appears in the whole record.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate software_and_tools with the named processing software and versions used to convert device exports and to build the OMOP CDM mapping, and point each entry at the AI-READI GitHub repository that implements it

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified carries two readings of the same fact without reconciling them. The method text says 'No active de-identification was necessary because no identifiers were collected' and, in the same field, that the public set 'is stripped of Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule via the Safe Harbor method'. deidentification_details then reports the FAIRhub deIdentType as 'NoDeIdentification' with deIdentHIPAA true. Whether Safe Harbor was applied to collected data or was a verification that no identifiers existed is left ambiguous, and the entry carries no source_caveats naming the tension.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a source_caveats note on is_deidentified distinguishing the checked-nothing-to-remove claim from the applied-Safe-Harbor claim, as the record does for the publisher, sampling and IRB conflicts

issues_detected.description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is 'restricted' while confidential_elements_present and sensitive_elements_present are both false. The two are reconcilable (access control on a release with no confidential content) and the record's own source_caveats concedes that both enum values are its mapping rather than a bundle statement, but nothing links the two slots so a reader meeting them separately sees a contradiction.
issues_detected.recommendation: Cross-reference the confidentiality_level caveat from confidential_elements so the access-control reading of 'restricted' is visible where the negative is asserted

issues_detected.description: data_protection_impacts is absent from the record. The relevant fact is recorded, but only in free-text notes: 'no data protection impact analysis has been conducted'. The same paragraph parks five further healthsheet negatives (no external audit, no use of the dataset at release, no repository of papers using it, no extension mechanism, no labeling guidelines) that no structured slot carries.
issues_detected.recommendation: Carry documented negatives in the slots they answer rather than in a prose notes block, so a consumer querying data_protection_impacts sees the 'none conducted' answer rather than nothing

issues_detected.description: The errata and release_notes slots are unused. Change information is real but scattered: version_access.version_details records the Snellen-to-logMAR drop, the increase in imaging devices and the new recommended split; updates.update_details points at the CHANGELOG; distribution_dates carries the three release dates. No erratum is asserted and none is denied.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate errata with an explicit 'no errata issued for this release' statement and release_notes with the CHANGELOG summary, so version tracking does not depend on reading version_details prose

issues_detected.description: The top-level license slot carries the free-text label 'AI-READI custom license v2.0'. The resolvable identifier for that license, doi:10.5281/zenodo.17555036, appears only inside license_and_use_terms.license_terms prose and inside ip_restrictions.notes. A consumer reading the license slot alone gets a name that resolves to nothing.
issues_detected.recommendation: Carry the Zenodo DOI of the license agreement in the license slot alongside the version label

issues_detected.description: The seven keywords cover disease, methods and modalities (Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam) but omit the program and dataset names that a searcher would most plausibly use: 'AI-READI', 'Bridge2AI', 'salutogenesis', 'OMOP', 'multimodal'. Program association is recoverable only from funders and the grant title.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add AI-READI, Bridge2AI, salutogenesis, OMOP Common Data Model and multimodal to keywords so program-level and standards-level discovery works from the keyword index alone

issues_detected.description: total_size_bytes is 3,815,969,779,678 while the nine datatype directory sizes sum to 3,815,969,360,064, a shortfall of 419,614 bytes. The record itself discloses the arithmetic in source_caveats, states the published total, and notes that the difference is plausibly the root metadata files but is accounted for by no source. Reported as a disclosed residual, not as an error the record introduced.
issues_detected.recommendation: None required; the disclosure is the correct handling. Retain the caveat rather than silently reconciling the figure

semantic_insights: Every published count in the record reconciles exactly. Race/ethnicity (380 + 545 + 519 + 836), sex (951 + 1,329) and diabetes severity (776 + 560 + 686 + 258) each sum to the 2,280 instances; the recommended splits (1,576 + 352 + 352) sum to 2,280; and each split's own race, sex and diabetes cells sum both across the split and down to the cohort total. No cell is off by one anywhere in subsets, subpopulations or instances.

The nine datatype file counts sum to 356,334, exactly 9 short of the stated total_file_count of 356,343, and the record identifies the nine root-level CDS metadata files as the difference. File-count arithmetic closes even where the byte arithmetic does not.

The DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3 uses the FAIRhub prefix and matches the FAIRhub publisher, the fairhub.io/datasets/3 landing page and the version_access DOIs 10.60775/fairhub.1 and .2, so the identifier, platform and version history are mutually consistent. The license DOI prefix 10.5281 is Zenodo, matching the record's separate Zenodo community resource.

Identifiers are written in CURIE form throughout (doi:10.60775/fairhub.3 for id and subset ids, ROR:01yc7t268, ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, B2AI_TOPIC:43), with resolver URLs reserved for uri-ranged slots such as page and access_urls. No resolver URL is misplaced into an identifier slot.

The three NIH grant numbers all match NIH structure: OT2OD032644 (OT2 other-transaction activity code, OD institute), P30DK035816 (center grant, NIDDK) and UL1TR003096 (CTSA, NCATS). The record additionally catches and corrects a source transcription error, recording the healthsheet's 'OT2ODO32644' as a transcription of OT2OD032644 rather than carrying the malformed string.

Human-subjects logic is fully closed: involves_human_subjects true is matched by irb_approval (University of Washington STUDY00016228, initial approval 20 December 2022, reliance agreements with UAB and UCSD), by informed_consent with consent type, documentation, scope and withdrawal mechanism, by collection_consents, and by consent_revocations recording that withdrawn participants' already-shared data remain in the dataset.

Deidentification is semantically appropriate to the data type. HIPAA Safe Harbor plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications is a defensible posture for a public multimodal clinical release, and the residual risk the record names (AI inference of individual characteristics) is the risk this modality mix actually carries. Mitigations are matched to it: watermarking, a two-tier release, license prohibitions on re-identification and contact, and privacy-first device selection with no audio, video, GPS or phone syncing.

Temporal ordering is coherent: collection 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01, then issued 2025-11-17, with the three release dates (2024-05-03, 2024-11-08, 2025-11-17) and their participant counts (204, 1,067, 2,280) increasing monotonically.

The record resolves rather than suppresses source conflict. Sampling is set is_sample true against the healthsheet's 'all possible instances' answer, on the strength of the registered Non-Probability Sample method and the documented wave-based EHR-screened recruitment, and the reasoning is written into the entry. The publisher, principal-investigator affiliation, name expansion, collection start date, target enrollment and NIH RePORTER project-identifier conflicts each get the same treatment in source_caveats.

The 13 collection_mechanisms entries are replication-grade: each names manufacturer and city, the acquisition protocol, the scan or wear duration, the export format and the standard it is converted to. Privacy rationale is attached where it drove the choice, and industry in-kind support is disclosed per device.

correctness_validations.doi_format: valid (10.60775/fairhub.3, FAIRhub prefix, consistent with the FAIRhub publisher, landing page and the 10.60775/fairhub.1 and .2 version DOIs; the license DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17555036 carries the Zenodo prefix and matches the record's Zenodo community resource; the two publication DOIs use the Springer Nature 10.1038 and BMJ 10.1136 prefixes)
correctness_validations.grant_number_format: valid (OT2OD032644, P30DK035816 and UL1TR003096 all match NIH activity-code plus institute plus serial structure; the healthsheet's mis-transcribed OT2ODO32644 is identified as such and not carried)
correctness_validations.url_validity: all_valid (fairhub.io/datasets/3 and /access, docs.aireadi.org, aireadi.org and /contact, github.com/AI-READI, zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, doi.org resolvers for the license and both publications, classic.clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT06002048, reporter.nih.gov project-details, and w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema are all well formed with plausible domains)

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3 ; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3 ; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3 with 10.60775/fairhub.1 and 10.60775/fairhub.2 for prior versions
sub_elements.quality_note: Format valid and prefix plausible: 10.60775 is FAIRhub's registered prefix and the record's publisher, landing page and version history all resolve to FAIRhub. The identifier is version-specific, and sibling version DOIs are carried, so a citation pins a release rather than a moving target.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description ~1,900 chars covering 2,280 adults aged 40+, three named US sites, the 19 July 2023 to 1 May 2025 collection window, every modality with its standard (OMOP, WFDB, DICOM, Open mHealth), the triple-balanced recruitment design, the salutogenesis goal and the public/controlled-access split
sub_elements.quality_note: Well above the 200-character bar and semantically matched to a multimodal clinical dataset. Every figure it states reappears in a structured slot, and it is candid about what the public version withholds rather than describing the study as if the whole cohort were released.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam
sub_elements.quality_note: Seven keywords, above the five-keyword threshold, spanning condition, method and three of the acquisition modalities. Weaker than the record's other discovery slots because it omits AI-READI, Bridge2AI, salutogenesis and OMOP, so program- and standard-level searches miss it (flagged low).

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 ; file_collections: ten typed collections (cardiac_ecg, clinical_data, environment, retinal_flio, retinal_oct, retinal_octa, retinal_photography, wearable_activity_monitor, wearable_blood_glucose, root metadata) each with id, path, collection_type, file_count, total_bytes and conforms_to; the root collection nests nine resources with format, media_type and file_type
sub_elements.quality_note: A live landing page plus a genuine two-level hierarchy: datatype directories with per-directory counts and byte sizes, and named files with media types beneath the metadata collection. A reuser can size and locate any modality before downloading anything.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2, is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.1, is_source_of 'AI-READI mini subset for pipeline development'; subsets: three split subsets with ids doi:10.60775/fairhub.3#split-train, #split-validation, #split-test and is_data_split true; was_derived_from names the AI-READI observational study
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationships are typed rather than listed, run both upward to prior versions and downward to the mini subset and the three splits, and each carries the participant counts that distinguish it. The mini subset entry honestly records that no DOI is stated for it.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: disease_specific_research, with ~2,000 chars of license terms naming Washington University in St. Louis as Licensor, the Authorized Group and Authorized User construction, the treatment of synthetic and derivative data as Data, the Licensee Model carve-out, the as-is warranty disclaimer and the one-dollar liability cap; ip_restrictions.restrictions: four entries covering title retention, reserved rights, separate publication licensing and the RO-Crate copyright notice
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the access policy and the intellectual-property position are stated in operational detail. The permission enum matches the license text (public version restricted to T2DM research), and the record notes the FAIRhub pages' looser 'Health Data License' label rather than adopting it.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; three regulatory_restrictions entries covering the NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy security standards, applicable-law compliance and the watermarking obligation; other_compliance records the study as not FDA-regulated for drugs or devices with no human-subject exemption claimed
sub_elements.quality_note: Both enums populated with a candid source_caveats stating that they are the record's own mapping rather than bundle statements, that the bundle's only confidentiality value is the RO-Crate's 'HL7:2N (normal)', and that no source calls the dataset 'compliant'. Inference is declared rather than presented as a source fact.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats access_urls: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 and https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access; data_governance.access_review_process: verified-ID login, agreement to use the data only for T2DM-related research, and acceptance of the license, with the FAIRhub access type recorded as PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired; third_party_sharing.is_shared true with the onward-sharing bound stated
sub_elements.quality_note: No dedicated download_url slot, but the platform link and the exact access procedure are both present, which is what the sub-element asks for. The conditions page is given separately from the dataset page, and the controlled-access route via a data use agreement is named.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: five entries giving application/dicom, JSON/application/json, CSV/text/csv, MD/text/markdown and a delivery entry naming the FAIRhub platform, the mini-subset version and Azure Storage access; file_collections carry per-directory conforms_to_standard values (CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH); the root resources list per-file format and media_type
sub_elements.quality_note: MIME types and format labels are both present and correct, and the record explains rather than fudges the gap where DICOM is not in the schema's format enum so only the media type is recorded. Per-modality format standards are recoverable from the file_collections even where distribution_formats aggregates.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: three typed entries (two prior versions, one mini subset); external_resources: seven annotated entries covering docs.aireadi.org, aireadi.org, github.com/AI-READI, the Zenodo community, the Nature Metabolism comment (10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x), the BMJ Open protocol (10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449) and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048
sub_elements.quality_note: Each external resource carries a note saying what it is and how the dataset metadata relates to it (IsDocumentedBy, associated publication, secondary identifier), and the documentation entry records its own CC-BY 4.0 licence. Publications are given by DOI with full citation, not bare links.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated with five entries and access_urls; page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 resolves to an accessible dataset page; license_and_use_terms grants a licence to download, reproduce, use and create derivative works for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'grants the Licensee a non-exclusive and non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the Data and to create derivative works of the Data, for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes'; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research; licensees may distribute Licensee Models trained on the Data provided the models do not contain the Data
sub_elements.quality_note: Not a standard SPDX licence, but the permissions, the scope limit to T2DM research on the public version, the derivative-work treatment and the model-redistribution carve-out are all stated explicitly enough for a reuser to know what they may do.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared-and-available condition as sub-element 1: distribution_formats and access_urls populated, landing page accessible, licence permits reuse
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH; conforms_to prose maps each standard to its datatype directory; distribution_formats give media types; file_collections repeat conforms_to per directory; distribution_formats notes 'All data files are in formats accessible with free software commonly used for such data types'
sub_elements.quality_note: Every modality is bound to a named community format standard, and the record states the conversion path from each proprietary device export into it. The encoding slot is unused, but character encoding is a minor gap next to six named format standards resolved to directory level.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared-and-available condition as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: Clinical Dataset Structure (CDS) v0.1.1 layout described directory by directory, with per-datatype format standards and the RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT / FAIRSCAPE profile 0.1 metadata package; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; clinical_data described as a one-to-one mapping to OMOP CDM tables
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is versioned (CDS v0.1.1, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT, FAIRSCAPE 0.1) rather than named loosely, and the notes explain why the RO-Crate is carried in conforms_to prose instead of conforms_to_standard: it describes the release from outside and is not one of the nine root files.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared-and-available condition as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: variables: 14 entries including participant_id (data_type identifier, is_identifier true, derivation given), HbA1c, Glucose, C peptide, Insulin, Troponin-T, urine albumin and creatinine, MoCA total score, best-corrected visual acuity (logMAR), letter contrast sensitivity, continuous glucose measurement and particulate matter concentration, each with data_type, unit where applicable, measurement_technique and reference ranges or scoring rules in notes
sub_elements.quality_note: The identifier variable is flagged as such and its derivation explained, and each measured variable carries the instrument that produced it plus the laboratory reference range. Necessarily a selection rather than a full data dictionary for a dataset of this size, but the entries chosen are the analytically load-bearing ones and each is complete.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Not conditional; scored for every record
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: three use_category entries with usage_notes and examples (T2DM AI/ML research, disease trajectory modelling, model training with the recommended splits); prohibited_uses: eight entries each pairing the prohibition with its prohibition_reason, covering clinical decision-making, re-identification and contact, third-party model-vendor sharing, onward conveyance, bulk reproduction in publications, non-T2DM research, watermark removal and non-compliant storage
sub_elements.quality_note: Unusually operational. Each prohibition states the rule and why it exists, and the AI-specific ones (vendor training versus short-term prompting, memorisation minimisation for redistributed models) are the boundaries a machine-learning reuser actually needs drawn. The discouraged_uses slot is unused, a minor gap.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: description (E1) states the dataset was 'collected from 2,280 adults aged 40 and older with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus' across three named clinical sites; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes recruitment and study visits with clinical research coordinators; regulatory_restrictions (E2) records confidentiality_level restricted with NIH GDS security obligations
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research.irb_approval: 'University of Washington IRB protocol STUDY00016228, with initial approval received on 20 December 2022', reliance agreements with UAB and UCSD IRBs using the same consent form; ethics_review_board names the reviewing body, the IRB Reliance Team contact and the Human Subjects Division postal address; ethical_reviews carries three entries (the UW IRB, four named ethicists recorded by the RO-Crate without a committee, and an 11-person Community Advisory Board)
sub_elements.quality_note: Protocol number, approval date, renewal obligation and multi-site reliance structure are all present, and the record flags the RO-Crate's 'Washington University IRB' label as conflicting with the University of Washington address it gives. data_protection_impacts is unused, though notes records that no DPIA was conducted (flagged low).

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human-subjects and governance conditions as sub-element 1, evidenced from E1 description, E8 collection_mechanisms and E2 regulatory_restrictions
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.method: no identifiers collected, checked against US HIPAA, 'stripped of Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule via the Safe Harbor method'; identifiers_removed lists PHI under Safe Harbor plus sex, race/ethnicity and medications; deidentification_details records the FAIRhub deIdentType, deIdentDirect, deIdentHIPAA and k-anonymity flags and the anti-stigmatisation rationale
sub_elements.quality_note: A named standard (HIPAA Safe Harbor), an explicit removed-identifier list and the platform's own de-identification metadata are all present, and Safe Harbor is the appropriate standard for a US clinical release of this kind. The method text carries an unreconciled tension between 'no de-identification was necessary' and 'stripped via Safe Harbor' (flagged low).

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human-subjects and governance conditions as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (study-ID folder naming, static watermarking, the two-tier public/controlled release, licence prohibitions on re-identification and contact, privacy-first device selection with no audio, video, GPS or phone syncing, HIPAA BAA storage requirements), reidentification_risk ('a theoretical risk of future re-identification is acknowledged; AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics'), data_linkage (Risk Level 3 plan, identifiers stored separately, no link in the released set)
sub_elements.quality_note: Risk is assessed rather than asserted away, and the named risk is the one this modality mix actually carries. Each protection maps to it. The assessment is qualitative with no residual-risk quantification, which is a real ceiling but consistent with what the sources support.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human-subjects and governance conditions as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent.consent_obtained true; consent_type: written consent by REDCap e-signature before the visit or in person at its start; consent_documentation: the approved UW form published with the dataset, reliance sites using it with institution-specific language, the signed form auto-emailed to the subject; consent_scope records the FAIRhub consent category and the public/private use asymmetry; withdrawal_mechanism permits withdrawal at any time; collection_consents and consent_revocations add the pre-consent e-consent flow and the retention of already-shared data on withdrawal
sub_elements.quality_note: The consent story is complete end to end: how consent was obtained, what document, what the participant received, what the consent permits downstream, how to withdraw, and the honest limit that withdrawal does not retract already-shared data. Both the consent and the IRB expectations of a human-subjects record are satisfied.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same human-subjects and governance conditions as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included false with special_protections naming the exclusions (pregnancy, gestational diabetes, type 1 diabetes, ages outside 40-85) and the IRB protocol's prisoner, fetus/neonate/pregnant-women and cognitively-impaired-adult determinations; participant_compensation: USD 200 stipend, not pro-rated, paid on device return, with parking, transit and rideshare cost coverage and the USD 25 reimbursement ceiling
sub_elements.quality_note: The negative is evidenced rather than asserted: each protected category is named with the eligibility rule or IRB determination that excludes it. Compensation gives amount, timing, rationale and the separate treatment of transport cost coverage as accessibility rather than incentive, and the notes distinguish project-level tribal-consultation commitments from the content of this release.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: three entries for race/ethnicity (Hispanic 380, Asian 545, Black 519, White 836), biological sex (male 951, female 1,329) and diabetes severity in four categories (776 / 560 / 686 / 258), each with identification, distribution, subpopulation_elements_present and notes; known_limitations and sampling_strategies give the 40-85 age band, English-language requirement and the pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 exclusions
sub_elements.quality_note: Demographics, inclusion and exclusion criteria and the recruitment balance targets are all present with counts. The subpopulation_elements_present flags correctly split false for race and sex, which are withheld from the public release, and true for diabetes status, which is released, with the asymmetry justified from the healthsheet and README.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances.counts: 2280 with instance_type defining an instance as all data for one participant across six modality groups; three subsets with is_data_split true giving 1,576 training, 352 validation and 352 test participants; total_file_count 356343 and total_size_bytes 3815969779678; per-collection file_count and total_bytes for all nine datatype directories; version history records 204 and 1,067 instances in prior versions
sub_elements.quality_note: Counts are given at participant, split, file and byte level, and every one of them reconciles: the split totals and all their demographic cells sum to 2,280, and the nine directory file counts sum to 9 short of the total, matching the nine root metadata files. The 419,614-byte size shortfall is disclosed rather than papered over.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: is_tabular: false; variables: 14 entries with variable_name, data_type, unit, measurement_technique, maximum_value where bounded, categories where enumerated, is_identifier on participant_id, and reference ranges or scoring rules in notes
sub_elements.quality_note: The tabular flag is correct for a release dominated by DICOM imaging and waveform data, and it is consistent with the file_collections, where only clinical_data is CSV-shaped. The variable entries are instrument-resolved rather than name-and-type stubs.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances.data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:43; instance_type enumerates the survey, clinical, retinal imaging, environmental sensor, CGM and wearable modalities; description and purposes name type 2 diabetes mellitus and salutogenesis; subpopulations define the four diabetes severity strata; file_collections describe each modality's clinical content
sub_elements.quality_note: The condition is carried both as a controlled topic identifier and in prose, and the modality coverage is enumerated per directory rather than summarised. A reuser can tell which clinical domains (metabolic, ophthalmic, cardiac, cognitive, environmental) the release actually spans.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: five entries covering skipped survey questions, wearable improper use and battery failure, imaging patient uncooperation and noise, data collisions causing loss, and the undilated handheld fundus camera's variable image quality; sampling_strategies documents the wave-based non-probability design and why it is not representative; missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling_strategy
sub_elements.quality_note: Anomalies are specific to the instrument that produces them, not generic. Missing data is decomposed into pattern, cause and treatment, and the record states that missing values fillable from elsewhere in a participant's record were filled while the rest were left missing or removed on PI review, with no instances excluded.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated with access_urls, page resolves to the FAIRhub dataset, licence permits reuse
sub_elements.evidence: version: 3.0.0; the version number also appears in the description, in version_access.versions_available and in the conforms_to RO-Crate reference to 'the 3.0.0 release and its nine sub-crates'
sub_elements.quality_note: Semantic version, consistent everywhere it appears, and bound to a version-specific DOI so the number and the identifier cannot drift apart.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.latest_version_doi doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; versions_available lists all three versions with DOI, release date and participant count; version_details records that each version has its own DOI and documentation set reachable from a version dropdown, and that versions 1.0.0 and 2.0.0 are no longer accessible through FAIRhub; notes gives the healthsheet URLs for the earlier versions
sub_elements.quality_note: Access to each version is described honestly, including the important negative that the two earlier releases have been withdrawn from the platform even though their DOIs and documentation persist. That is exactly the fact a reproducibility-minded reuser needs and the one most records omit.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.version_details: 'the data fields and types are largely the same, except that the Snellen visual acuity variables were dropped so that only logMAR visual acuity measurements are available; the number of image devices increased across releases and a recommended data split was added'; updates.update_details points to the CHANGELOG file included in the dataset and visible at docs.aireadi.org; the logMAR variable entry repeats the Snellen drop; distribution_dates gives the three release dates
sub_elements.quality_note: Concrete, specific change descriptions at field level, not a pointer to a changelog alone. The dedicated errata and release_notes slots are unused and no explicit 'no errata' statement is made, which is the gap keeping this from being unambiguous (flagged low).

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: 'Approximately once a year'; update_details: released as static versions and not updated in place, with new versions carrying participants enrolled since the last release, enrolment ongoing and future versions expected to be larger
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the cadence and the update model are stated. The static-versioning statement is the more useful half: it tells a reuser that a pinned DOI will not change under them, which the observed 2024-05, 2024-11 and 2025-11 release dates corroborate.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: was_derived_from: the AI-READI observational study; raw_data_sources: two entries distinguishing direct prospective collection from participants and existing clinical records from the three health systems, the latter with access_details noting the derived variables are controlled-access only; raw_sources details the device-native formats before standardisation and states the raw data are preserved for the project's duration but not currently shared and why
sub_elements.quality_note: Provenance runs from study to raw device export to standardised release, and separates the two upstream source types with different access consequences. The raw_sources entry is candid that raw data may carry PHI in free-text fields and so are withheld, with a possibility of inclusion in future controlled-access releases.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: three responses covering AI/ML insight into T2DM and salutogenic pathways, enabling downstream pseudotime manifold analysis to reconstruct a temporal atlas of T2DM development and reversal, and establishing standards and best practices for AI-ready data as a blueprint for future projects; addressing_gaps: three responses naming the absence of AI-ready multimodal datasets for multi-organ disease, the under-representation of higher-burden racial and ethnic groups documented in a 2000-2020 meta-epidemiological review, and the infeasibility of these analyses on claims or EHR data
sub_elements.quality_note: Purpose and the gap it addresses are stated separately and both are specific. The gap statements cite the evidence behind them rather than asserting a need, and they explain the design choices (triple-balanced recruitment, multimodal acquisition) that follow from them.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: pseudotime manifold analysis to predict disease trajectories across severity strata from normal to insulin-dependent T2DM, and AI/ML model development on a hypothesis-agnostic multimodal dataset using the recommended 70/15/15 split distributed with the release
sub_elements.quality_note: Named analytic methods rather than a generic 'machine learning' claim, and the second task is tied to a concrete artefact shipped in the release (participants.tsv split assignments). Consistent with instances.label false and the hypothesis-agnostic framing in label_description.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: National Institutes of Health with the mechanism named ('made through the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program', award title 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project'), plus Research to Prevent Blindness; notes record the healthsheet's funding statement and its grant-number transcription; the record's own notes list in-kind support from the Microsoft AI for Good Lab, device loans from Topcon, Optomed, iCare World and Carl Zeiss, and research discounts from Heidelberg Engineering, Dexcom and Garmin
sub_elements.quality_note: Agency, programme and mechanism are all present, and the in-kind support is separated from grant funding rather than conflated with it. The device-vendor relationships are disclosed both here and per device in collection_mechanisms notes.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders[0].grants: OT2OD032644 with NIH RePORTER application 10471118, project number 1OT2OD032644-01, fiscal year 2022, award amount USD 5,026,499 and the 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31 project period; P30DK035816 and UL1TR003096 each noted as named in the protocol publication but absent from the dataset's own funding reference
sub_elements.quality_note: All three match NIH structure: OT2/OD, P30/DK and UL1/TR with valid serials. The record catches the healthsheet's mis-transcription 'OT2ODO32644' and records it as a transcription of the correct number, and it flags the two divergent RePORTER project-detail identifiers (10885481 versus 10471118) for the same core project rather than silently choosing one.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: AI-READI Consortium with nameType Organizational, affiliation Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) and principal_investigator Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, contact@aireadi.org) with two affiliations; created_by: AI-READI Consortium; source_caveats names the fifteen further study principal investigators and seven collaborating organisations and explains why they are recorded as study personnel rather than dataset creators; notes acknowledge the in-kind cloud and device support
sub_elements.quality_note: Creators carry persistent identifiers (ORCID, ROR) rather than plain names, and the boundary between dataset creator and study personnel is drawn explicitly with its reasoning. The two-source disagreement about the principal investigator's institution is represented rather than resolved by fiat.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified (acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms populated) and the datasets-shared condition met via distribution_formats, access_urls and a reuse-permitting licence
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: thirteen entries. REDCap for questionnaires and visit clinical data with out-of-range flagging; Philips PageWriter TC30 12-lead ECG with recorded recline angle; LeeLab Anura home environmental sensor with its ten-day placement protocol and full sensor list; Dexcom G6 CGM at five-minute sampling with participants masked; Garmin Vivosmart 5 at five-second sampling on the non-dominant wrist; five named retinal imaging platforms with field of view, scan protocol and room conditions; and a final entry enumerating in-clinic instruments down to the monofilament, lensometer and blood-pressure monitor models
sub_elements.quality_note: Replication-grade. Each entry names manufacturer and location, the acquisition protocol and its settings, the wear or scan duration, the export format and the standard it converts to, with privacy rationale attached where it drove device selection. collection_timeframes adds the 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 window and the pilot-versus-formal phase boundary.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same collection-identified and datasets-shared conditions as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: two entries, one with was_directly_observed and was_validated_verified true describing laboratory results, vital signs and retinal imaging with medication cross-referencing against physically presented or photographed medications, one with was_reported_by_subjects true enumerating the survey domains; raw_data_sources: prospective participant collection and existing EHR extraction, the latter with its controlled-access consequence; data_collectors: four roles with training, certification and quality-control responsibilities
sub_elements.quality_note: The observed/reported boundary is drawn with the schema's own booleans and then evidenced, and verification practice is described concretely rather than claimed. The data_collectors entries add who did what and what training and certification they held, which is what makes the acquisition account auditable.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: external_resources (E10) references the code repository https://github.com/AI-READI; purposes (E7) state that a goal of the dataset is 'to establish standards, best practices and guidelines for the collection, preparation and sharing of data for AI/ML purposes'
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: five entries covering OMOP CDM and DICOM standardisation for AI-readiness, the .fda/.sdt/.FIT/.xml conversion paths, Safe Harbor PHI removal plus the sex, race/ethnicity and medication removals, the CDS v0.1.1 layout with manifest.tsv and the nine root metadata files including dqd_omop.json for the 3,500-plus OMOP quality checks, and the move from ad hoc v1.0.0 handling to automated processing for v2.0.0 and v3.0.0; cleaning_strategies: two entries on REDCap range-check review with PI-approved editing and on site data-manager quality control before upload; instances.label false with label_description explaining that no labelling was performed because the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic
sub_elements.quality_note: The processing pipeline is traceable from device export to released artefact, and the cleaning account names who could authorise an edit and what happened to uncorrectable values. The absence of labelling is documented as a deliberate design decision rather than left as a silent gap; labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses and imputation_protocols are unused but the negatives they would carry are stated.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same software-output condition as sub-element 3: github.com/AI-READI in external_resources and the standards-and-tooling purpose in E7
sub_elements.evidence: software_and_tools absent. Software named incidentally elsewhere: REDCap (capture, range-check reports, e-consent), the MoCA Duo iPad application, the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard via dqd_omop.json, https://github.com/AI-READI as an organisation link, and FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure as the hosting platform. No version number appears for any software anywhere in the record, and the described conversions (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth, .xml to WFDB, clinical data to OMOP CDM) name no converting tool or repository
sub_elements.quality_note: The dedicated slot is empty and, more importantly, the sub-element's purpose is unmet: a reuser cannot tell what software produced this release. The GitHub link is an organisation URL, not a repository tied to a processing step, and the incidentally named tools are data-capture and quality-checking software rather than the conversion pipeline (flagged medium).

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met via distribution_formats, access_urls and a reuse-permitting licence
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: seven entries including the BMJ Open protocol publication (10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449), the Nature Metabolism comment (10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x), ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048, docs.aireadi.org with its CC-BY 4.0 terms, aireadi.org, github.com/AI-READI and the Zenodo community; conforms_to and conforms_to_standard name CDS v0.1.1, WFDB, OMOP CDM, the NASA ESDS guidelines, DICOM, Open mHealth, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT and FAIRSCAPE 0.1; sensor component datasheets (AS7431, DS3231, Sensirion SEN5x) are referenced in the environment collection
sub_elements.quality_note: Standards are named with versions and bound to the directories they govern, and the external references are annotated with what each is and how the dataset metadata relates to it. Publications are given by DOI with full citations, and the trial registration is identified as a secondary identifier of the parent study.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: five typed entries. representativeness_limitation (urban, hospital-based recruitment excluding Pacific Islanders and Native Americans) with scope_impact naming the generalisation boundary; coverage_limitation (not all modalities for all participants); scope_limitation (public version withholds sex, race/ethnicity, medications, zip code, genetic data, past records and traffic reports) with recommended_mitigation naming the data use agreement; temporal_limitation (cross-sectional, one visit, no within-participant longitudinal analysis); scope_limitation (age 40-85, English-language, pregnancy and type 1 exclusions)
sub_elements.quality_note: Each limitation carries a type from the schema's vocabulary, and the two that admit a workaround carry the workaround. The scope_impact statements say what conclusions the limitation actually forecloses rather than restating the limitation.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: four entries using BiasTypeEnum values selection_bias (volunteer bias), representation_bias (urban hospital-based recruitment, no Pacific Islanders or Native Americans) with mitigation_strategy naming the three geographically selected sites, sampling_bias (interim releases not balanced across the three parameters) with affected_subsets and a mitigation_strategy describing uniform protocols across sites and strata, and a second selection_bias entry on the English-language eligibility requirement and its documented effect on Hispanic and Asian recruitment; future_use_impacts: two entries on AI-enabled re-identification risk and on residual imbalance in this interim release
sub_elements.quality_note: Four structured bias types with descriptions, and three of the four carry a mitigation or an affected-subset scope. The English-language finding is the kind of self-implicating detail records usually omit, and future_use_impacts supplies the downstream social-impact dimension the sub-element asks for.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: five entries covering skipped or incomplete survey responses, wearable improper use and battery failure with named Garmin charging gaps, imaging patient uncooperation, obscuring noise, system malfunction and transfer failures, data collisions causing loss, and the Optomed Aurora's patient-to-patient and within-patient image quality variation attributed to undilated handheld acquisition; missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling_strategy
sub_elements.quality_note: Anomalies are attributed to the specific instrument or process that generates them, and the fundus-camera entry explains the physical cause of the quality variation. Paired with missing_data_documentation, a reuser can anticipate which modality will be sparse and why.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: content_warnings: content_warnings_present false with the healthsheet question quoted in the note; sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present false with sensitivity_details enumerating the sensitive variables the study collected (race and ethnicity, 5-digit zip code, motor vehicle accident reports, genetic sequencing data, past health records, medications) and stating they are withheld to the controlled-access version; confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present false with the RO-Crate's HL7:2N confidentiality level recorded
sub_elements.quality_note: Both negatives are evidenced rather than asserted, and the sensitive_elements entry does the harder thing: it names what sensitive data exists in the study and explains that its absence from this release is the reason the flag is false. That is the information a reuser needs to know a controlled tier exists.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: three entries. The University of Washington IRB with protocol STUDY00016228, approval date, reliance scope, renewal obligation and the published approval letter, plus source_caveats on the RO-Crate's conflicting 'Washington University IRB' label; a second entry recording ethical review by four named individuals (Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman, Nicholas Evans) with source_caveats explaining that no organisation is recorded because the bundle attaches none; the AI-READI Community Advisory Board of 11 members from the three sites evaluating consent forms and protocols. Commercial-interest disclosure appears in license_and_use_terms.notes (no plans for commercial products or patents by the collecting researchers) and in the per-device notes recording loans and discounts from Topcon, Optomed, iCare, Zeiss, Heidelberg, Dexcom and Garmin
sub_elements.quality_note: Review is documented at three levels (institutional, ethicist, community) with the boundary of each stated. No dedicated conflict-of-interest slot is populated, but the industry relationships that would populate one are disclosed device by device and the researchers' commercialisation position is on record, so the sub-element's substance is met.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated with access_urls, page resolves to the FAIRhub dataset, licence permits reuse
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: https://fairhub.io/ ; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 ; maintainers records FAIRhub as 'a Microsoft Azure cloud-based data management, curation and sharing platform developed for this project, which also publishes the dataset and mints its DOIs'; source_caveats records that the FAIRhub API names FAIRhub as publisher while the RO-Crate names the AI-READI Consortium, and explains why the platform URI is carried
sub_elements.quality_note: A recognised repository with DOI-minting capability, and its role is described rather than merely named. The tier-1 publisher conflict is surfaced with the reasoning for the choice instead of being resolved silently. The slot carries a URL rather than a name, a minor form issue that does not affect identification.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publication identified: external_resources carries the BMJ Open protocol (10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449) and the Nature Metabolism comment (10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x); datasets-shared condition met as above
sub_elements.evidence: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3'; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; license_and_use_terms requires acknowledgement of the Licensor, source and funder following the citation instructions at docs.aireadi.org
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete DataCite-style citation carrying creator, year, title, version, resource type, repository and resolvable DOI, consistent with the identifier slots. The licence-level attribution obligation reinforces it, and the two associated publications give the cross-reference targets.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH; conforms_to describes the CDS v0.1.1 directory hierarchy and binds each standard to its datatype directory, and names the RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT package conforming to FAIRSCAPE profile 0.1; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; file_collections repeat conforms_to and conforms_to_standard per directory
sub_elements.quality_note: Six community standards plus two metadata-packaging profiles, all versioned and each bound to the part of the release it governs. This is standards conformance stated at the granularity a downstream integrator can act on rather than a list of acronyms.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: https://docs.aireadi.org/ with per-version documentation sets and its CC-BY 4.0 terms, https://aireadi.org/ hosting the team listing and contact page, https://github.com/AI-READI, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi; page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; maintainers give https://aireadi.org/contact, https://docs.aireadi.org/docs/3/contact and contact@aireadi.org; version_access links the v1 and v2 healthsheets
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation, project site, code organisation, community archive and multiple contact routes, each annotated with what it holds. The healthsheet's own admission that the dataset is self-contained but relies on the documentation for provenance detail is carried, which is the honest framing of what these links are for.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 (1,067 participants, 8 November 2024, no longer accessible), is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.1 (204 participants, 3 May 2024, pilot phase, no longer accessible), is_source_of 'AI-READI mini subset for pipeline development' noting the FAIRhub child dataset identifier 4 and that no DOI is stated for the subset
sub_elements.quality_note: Every relationship is typed with a controlled value and targets a resolvable DOI where one exists, with the participant deltas and the withdrawal status attached. The mini-subset entry states plainly that no DOI is available rather than fabricating one.

strengths: Numerical self-consistency is complete. Race/ethnicity, sex and diabetes-severity counts each sum to the 2,280 instances, the three recommended splits sum to 2,280, and every demographic cell inside each split reconciles both across the split and down to the cohort total. The nine datatype file counts sum to exactly 9 short of the stated total, matching the nine root metadata files the record itself names.

Collection is documented at replication grade. Thirteen collection_mechanisms entries name manufacturer, location, acquisition protocol, settings, duration, export format and conversion target for every instrument, from the Philips ECG and Dexcom G6 down to the monofilament and the lensometer models, with privacy rationale attached where it drove device selection.

Ethics documentation is closed end to end. involves_human_subjects true is matched by a named IRB protocol with approval date and multi-site reliance structure, by consent covering type, documentation, scope, withdrawal and the honest limit that withdrawn participants' shared data remain, by a Safe Harbor de-identification account with an identifiers-removed list, and by a re-identification risk assessment whose named risk fits the modality mix.

Source conflict is resolved in the open. Publisher, principal-investigator affiliation, IRB label, name expansion, collection start date, target enrolment, version scope, sampling design and the two NIH RePORTER project identifiers each get a caveat naming both readings and the reasoning for the value carried, rather than a silent choice.

Reuse boundaries are operational. Eight prohibited_uses entries each pair the rule with its reason, and the AI-specific ones draw the lines a machine-learning reuser actually needs: vendor model training versus short-term prompting, synthetic data treated as Data, and a memorisation-minimisation duty on redistributed models.
weaknesses: The software_and_tools slot is empty and no software version appears anywhere in the record. The described conversions from Topcon .fda, Heidelberg .sdt, Garmin .FIT and ECG .xml into DICOM, Open mHealth and WFDB name no converting tool, so a reuser cannot tell what produced the release.

is_deidentified carries two readings of the same fact without reconciling them: that no active de-identification was necessary because no identifiers were collected, and that the public set was stripped of PHI via HIPAA Safe Harbor. The FAIRhub deIdentType 'NoDeIdentification' with deIdentHIPAA true sits between them and no caveat names the tension.

Six documented healthsheet negatives (no DPIA, no external audit, no recorded uses at release, no repository of papers using the dataset, no extension mechanism, no labelling guidelines) live only in a free-text notes paragraph. data_protection_impacts in particular is a slot a consumer would query and find empty.

The errata and release_notes slots are unused. Change information is real but distributed across version_details, updates and known_limitations, and no explicit statement that no errata were issued for this release is made.

Keywords omit the terms a searcher is most likely to use for this dataset: AI-READI, Bridge2AI, salutogenesis, OMOP and multimodal. Program association is recoverable only from the funders block and the grant title.
recommendations: Populate software_and_tools with the named conversion and mapping software and their versions, each linked to the AI-READI repository that implements it, so the pipeline from device export to released artefact is attributable.

Add a source_caveats note on is_deidentified separating the no-identifiers-collected claim from the Safe-Harbor-applied claim, in the same style the record already uses for the publisher and sampling conflicts.
Move the healthsheet negatives out of the notes paragraph into the slots they answer, starting with data_protection_impacts recording that no impact analysis was conducted.
Populate errata with an explicit no-errata statement for version 3.0.0 and release_notes with the CHANGELOG summary, so version tracking does not depend on reading version_details prose.
Extend keywords with AI-READI, Bridge2AI, salutogenesis, OMOP Common Data Model and multimodal, and carry the licence DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17555036 in the license slot alongside the version label.
